notes:
CRM-style notes / call snippets:
- Company: RivetLane — mid-market B2B SaaS (support automation). Primary product: conversational support agents that perform multi-step actions (search KB, call orchestration service, create/update CRM tickets, trigger customer-facing emails).
- POC objective: validate Hosted API for production chat agents with strict latency SLOs (p95 < 400ms for streaming token delivery; end-to-end action completion < 2s for simple tool calls).
- They ran demo with streaming + function/tool calling; liked streaming latency and partial response streaming. Quote from PM: "Streaming makes the UI feel real-time, but when a tool call stalls the whole agent blocks."
- Key technical concerns noted repeatedly: tool-call reliability & timeouts (HTTP tool endpoints occasionally 504), retry semantics (idempotency), KV/prefix cache behavior across multi-step flows, and how Redwood handles mid-agent fallback when a tool fails.
- Cost sensitivity: multi-step agents amplify token counts; they want better unit-economics and concrete batching/caching guidance from Redwood Optimize. Interested in model/quantization recs for chat-heavy workloads.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 must, SSO/SAML for product team; KMS + audit logs for ticketing updates. Some EU customers require data residency — legal will need Private or Dedicated with regional routing.
- Sales/contract: leaning Hosted API for MVP (fast), but evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation once POC passes. AE shared Dedicated pricing ranges; finance is modeling 12-month commit.
- Demo/POC results: baseline chat latency acceptable at low concurrency; at 50-100 concurrent agents saw increased tool-call failures and streaming stalls. SE workaround: increase client-side timeouts + server-side retries; not ideal.
- Action items (from meetings): SE to run a 100-concurrent soak test on Dedicated staging (if pricing agreeable), provide SAML quickstart guide, share Optimize runbook for batching/caching, escalate INF-1423 for detailed trace capture.
- Sales note: decision influenced by whether Redwood can show predictable p95 latency under 100 concurrent agents and an SSO/KMS integration timeline that works for their compliance deadline.
